summary:
Project D.A.I.S.Y. is an educational resource-management game in which players take the role of an astronaut tasked with restoring and operating an abandoned Martian outpost alongside D.A.I.S.Y. (Dynamic Autonomous Intelligence for Space & You), an AI assistant designed to help maintain the colony. Players must manage interconnected systems such as oxygen production, hydroponic food cultivation, water recycling and power generation through exploration, repairs, and resource management.

The game addresses the challenge by transforming real engineering constraints into interactive gameplay. Players face dust storms that reduce solar output, oxygen leaks that threaten life support, equipment failures and limited energy reserves. Every decision affects multiple systems, demonstrating the trade-offs faced by real astronauts and mission planners. Conserving one resource often comes at the expense of another, teaching players that survival on Mars depends on balancing competing needs rather than finding perfect solutions.

This project is important because it helps younger audiences understand the complexity of sustaining human life beyond Earth through hands-on decision-making rather than memorisation. By turning real-world challenges into engaging gameplay, Project D.A.I.S.Y. aims to spark interest in STEM, sustainability, problem-solving, and future space exploration.
details:
Our project is an educational resource-management game developed in Godot that teaches players about the challenges of sustaining human life on Mars. Players are tasked with restoring and maintaining an abandoned Martian outpost while managing critical systems such as oxygen production, power generation, water recycling, heating, and food production.

The gameplay is focused on demonstrating how interconnected life-support systems are in a space habitat. Resources are limited, and every decision has consequences. Players must respond to events such as dust storms, oxygen leaks and equipment failures, all while ensuring the colony remains operational. Many of these situations are inspired by real challenges that engineers and mission planners must consider when designing future Mars missions.

To make these concepts engaging for younger audiences, the game combines resource management with simple interactive minigames. When a system fails, the player must physically travel through the base and repair it by completing short maintenance challenges. D.A.I.S.Y. (Dynamic Autonomous Intelligence for Space & You), the station's AI assistant, then explains the consequences of the player's actions and how they affect the colony's resources. This approach allows players to learn through experimentation and observation rather than simply reading information.

A key design goal was ensuring that no decision is completely free. Conserving one resource often requires sacrificing another, encouraging players to think critically about trade-offs. For example, maintaining food production may require diverting power away from other systems, while repairing external equipment may consume valuable oxygen reserves. By connecting all major systems together, the game demonstrates the complexity of keeping a Mars habitat operational.

The project also includes multiple endings that depend on the player's choices and overall management of the colony. Success is determined not only by surviving but also by how effectively players maintain the outpost and complete mission objectives.

We developed the game using the Godot Engine. Visual assets were created in Procreate, while audio and music were sourced from royalty-free resources available on Pixabay. Throughout development, we focused on creating an experience that is easy for younger players to understand while still introducing authentic space exploration concepts.

Our intended impact is to spark interest in STEM fields and space exploration by presenting real engineering challenges in a fun and approachable way. We hope players leave with a better understanding of the systems required to support human life beyond Earth, as well as the importance of careful planning, resource management, and problem-solving.
